transport: Modbus RTU · 9600 8N1 · default slave 1 (range 0x01–0xF7; 0x00 broadcast, 0xF8 general). Physical layer forks by model: PZEM-014/016 are RS-485; PZEM-004T v3.0 is 5 V TTL UART and needs its own converter — it cannot join an RS-485 bus as sold.
blocks: Input registers 0x0000–0x0009 read with FC 0x04 (measurement) · holding 0x0001 power alarm threshold @1 W and 0x0002 Modbus address, FC 0x03 read / FC 0x06 write · FC 0x42 reset energy · FC 0x41 calibration, 0xF8 only, password 0x3721 · CRC-16 poly 0xA001

gotchas: This survey UPGRADES the existing driver's confidence. crates/drivers/cabin-pzem/src/pzem_016.rs documents itself as cross-checked against a community library because no vendor PDF was in hand. Two vendor PDFs are now committed and they confirm every address, scale, and the 8N1 framing. The module doc-comment should be
8N1, against the DC meters' 8N2, at the same 9600 baud. Same-baud/different-framing is the failure that looks like a wiring fault and is not. A 016 needs its own adapter, not a share of the 017s'.

Current is 0.001 A/LSB here but 0.01 A/LSB on the DC meters, and current is a 32-bit pair here but a single register there. The two PZEM halves do not share a map; nothing about the AC table can be reused on a 017.
Both AC tables put the LOW word at the LOWER address for the 32-bit quantities. That is the meter's order, not a convention to assume.

CONTRADICTION inside the vendor doc: the PZEM-004T V3.0 manual's overview says 'the data is read through the TTL interface' and §5.1 says 'The TTL interface of this module is a passive interface', but §1.8 says 'RS485 interface' and §2.1 says 'Physical layer use UART to RS485 communication interface' — both left unedit
unmappedReports: Over-power alarm status (0x0009, 0xFFFF = alarm) — no MetricKind for a device-side alarm flag. cabin-pzem reads the register (block count 0x0A) and deliberately drops it., Power alarm threshold (holding 0x0001, 1 W/LSB) — settable over the wire, no CommandKind covers setting a device threshold
